text:
The response provides a basic structural comparison of US and Chinese antitrust frameworks but has significant shortcomings. It completely omits the requested case studies, contains factual inaccuracies regarding enforcement agency jurisdictions (e.g., the FTC/DOJ and SAMR/MOFCOM splits are mischaracterized), and presents a confused statutory comparison (the Sherman Act does address monopolization; the Clayton Act covers mergers, making the "difference" claims misleading). It lacks depth on legal standards (rule of reason, per se rules, abuse of dominance tests), ignores major recent developments (China's 2022 AML amendments, US tech antitrust cases), and offers no analysis of substantive differences in approach. The response addresses only a fraction of the prompt with notable errors.

Rating: [[3]]
